title: Bind affinity policy to the successor interpretation model
author: Worldview Sorter AI editorial review
currentBehavior: The six-entry catalog policy binds generic-1.1.0-pilot.
proposedBehavior: Bind the seven-entry catalog to generic-1.2.0-pilot without changing qualitative affinity state semantics.
rationale: Comparison inputs must be exact interpreted propositions from the matching model version.

philosophicalBasis.proposition: Some existence questions can be settled by conceptual application conditions and relevant empirical facts without a further special metaphysical test.
neighboringViews: Ordinary-object realism without an easy-ontology method
nonEntailments: An established view about realism compatibility
philosophicalBasis.existingGap: The existing scoped OM14 rule has only a legacy label and no rule-linked claim.
philosophicalBasis.scholarlyDisagreement: Marschall challenges whether Thomasson can preserve realism while making ontological questions easy.

sourceClaims.claim: Marschall describes Easy Ontology as settling many ontological questions through conceptual truths and empirical knowledge, while disputing whether its defense of realism succeeds.

alternatives: Add the entire draft question pool: rejected because the existing OM14 items ask this narrow method directly.
Infer the method from ordinary-object realism: rejected because belief in objects does not settle metaontological method.
Retain an unqualified identity label: rejected because the pilot asks only a limited proposition.
respondentImpact: The added comparison uses the same qualitative overlap/divergence/missing states, never percentages or identity.
historicalCompatibility: The 1.3.0 model, six-entry catalog, route items, source ledger, and original results remain byte-identical. A new manifest pins the new model and catalog; old administrations replay under their recorded versions.

approvals.note: Reviewed the exact scoped claim, neighboring realism and nominalism positions, and source limits.
Reviewed historical version binding, route opportunity, and adversarial software fixtures.

release.migration: No raw-response migration. Historical model and affinity results retain their previous manifest; new administrations use the new tuple.
